chunk.text: I think the most attacking, dominant team in the world right now is Bayern Munich. Bayern Munich. They are too good. And I believe we have a very interactive... I saw a game in Atlanta because I wanted to understand them better. We don't see Bayern Munich much in league football; it is usually in Champions League matches where we watch them. So I made a small observation, and he was like... it's okay. I wanted to check my mic too. It's okay, you know. I could have told you, but you were hanging there for 5 seconds, so I didn’t say anything. It’s okay. Sorry, sorry. Don’t worry. Take the mic from him. Dogo bhai, I’ve got the mic. And you were talking about Bayern. So, boys, our theory is a little far-fetched.

No, I think... I just wanted to say that if a beautiful, superpower machine like Bayern—not even a team—if they can have players like Nicolas Jackson, who would have been criticized by Chelsea fans a year ago, and now you are saying he is playing well... and earlier you were criticizing him. It’s the same Rashford and Antony theory. When Antony went to Betis or Rashford at United... Hojlund, for example. When he went to Napoli, he was doing well. Take McTominay as well—I agree. So I just feel like... Muktesh will tell you that Bayern is such a super team that even players like Nicolas Jackson can start, and Bayern will still score 6 goals.

It’s crazy. Exactly, that’s a good point. Thank you so much, Yash, for the great start. Because the interesting thing I saw in the Atlanta match—this was something a Bayern fan told me—is that Harry Kane drops deep. That’s what he does. And the only thing he mentioned was that the most interesting factor about Bayern Munich's attack and their front three—Olise, their striker Harry Kane, and the left winger Luis Diaz—their numbers are so good. So the most important movement factor is which player’s?

If I ask you a general question about these three—who in Bayern's team has the key movement that is actually the reason these players are thriving so much? Is it the striker’s movement, the winger’s movement, the midfielder’s movement, or the fullback? Fullback. I think they have a beautiful enigma of a number 10 called Gnabry—he moves crazily. Gnabry, that’s a good shout. Yeah, fullbacks. I think it’s the midfield—Kimmich. Okay, so there’s a mix of opinions. But the simple and to-the-point answer is actually the fullbacks. Fullbacks—wow.

And that is a good point. Now, we hear the whole season that Bayern play their best game when Harry Kane plays—he drops, he releases balls, everything. But here, Bayern are masters at creating space in the opponent’s backline. Now, if we look at this, we’ll see many instances where the left winger and the striker pull defenders out. Gnabry moves, another defender is dragged, and space is created. Now, this space is not created just once—Bayern create this space multiple times, probably 10 times in a match.

Right. And you would expect this space to be created by many top teams like PSG or Barcelona, especially teams that play with a false 9 or use a number 10 to drive play. But Bayern do something slightly different. Here, the winger doesn’t move. Instead, their fullback makes a late run. The winger stays wide, the striker stays central, and the fullback runs into that space from deeper areas. For example, Stanisic comes into that space, and that’s what makes it effective.

If we see this instance, defenders leave the winger or striker because there’s a direct play towards goal. At that moment, the attacking trio are left free. That’s why many Bayern players score from outside the box as well. The defenders get pulled toward the fullback, space opens behind, and the ball is released into that space. And this doesn’t happen just once. If we move to the next example, we’ll again see the fullback’s movement creating space.

The striker pulls defenders away, the number 10—Musiala—moves into position. In another example, Alphonso Davies moves inwards. The defenders haven’t even reacted yet, but Davies arrives in a central position and waits. Now, PSG do something similar, but the difference is that PSG’s fullbacks—especially Hakimi—move like this, while Nuno Mendes often holds the width. In Bayern, both fullbacks move inward. The biggest difference is that Bayern’s fullbacks control the tempo—they hold the play and then release it.

So there are two triggers: first, the fullback moves and pauses, then they release the play. PSG’s fullbacks don’t wait—they attack immediately. And that’s why I feel the most interesting Champions League match this season, if it happens, will be PSG vs Bayern Munich. It could happen in the semi-finals. The reason is that in games like Dortmund, where Bayern struggled, it was because of how their midfield and positioning worked when players like Musiala and Kane dropped deep.

So here we see Gnabry or Musiala in advanced roles, while Harry Kane drops deeper. Now, the reason I say PSG vs Bayern would be the most interesting game is because Bayern’s fullbacks are crucial both offensively and defensively. Their midfielders contribute a lot, but against PSG’s midfield, they may not get that same leverage. And PSG’s fullbacks—Nuno Mendes and Hakimi—are among the best in Europe right now. I think Bayern’s biggest kryptonite this season could be PSG.

I think PSG are the only team that can defeat Bayern. Otherwise, if Bayern beat PSG, they could go on to win the Champions League. Fair point. What about Arsenal? I think Bayern’s players are performing so well individually that they are not entirely dependent on tactics. Give them space, and they will score. Arsenal, on the other hand, rely heavily on structure and defensive discipline, not leaving spaces.

I believe Bayern have players who can break that structure. I could be wrong, but if these two teams meet, it would likely be in the final. In that case, Bayern might have the edge. But again, there are multiple layers to this discussion. Personally, I’m really looking forward to PSG vs Bayern. Now, should we talk about Michael Olise? Absolutely. The next question is—if Olise wasn’t doing this, would the hype be the same?

Yes, exactly. If this was not being done by someone like Olise, the media narrative would be very different. If Olise goes on to win the Champions League, and France wins the World Cup—which they are capable of—then who becomes the Ballon d'Or favorite? Mbappe or Michael Olise? Logically speaking, Olise is having the best season of his career.

Whenever people talk about Olise, they say it’s just Bundesliga bias. But he was doing the same in the Premier League with Crystal Palace—scoring against big teams like United and delivering in big games alongside Eze. Now he has gone to Bayern and is doing the same. Harry Kane, if he had stayed in the Premier League, would still be the top scorer. Now he’s doing the same in the Bundesliga.

This is a top-quality player, and he is performing in the Champions League as well. The numbers he is producing are incredible. Aesthetically, everyone already knows he is world-class. Right now, he should definitely start for France—probably even ahead of Dembele. And I’ll say this directly—Florentino Perez should sign him.

He is that good. If I see a future Galactico in football right now, apart from Haaland, it’s Michael Olise. He has the potential to reach the top. If we talk about comparisons like Yamal vs Vinicius or Mbappe, then Olise should also be part of that conversation once he reaches that level.

He is one of the best one-on-one dribblers right now. Overall, his game is elite. It’s unfortunate that he isn’t widely recognized yet. But stats don’t depend on popularity—they depend on performance, and he is delivering. At the same time, we shouldn’t ignore what players like Luis Diaz are doing. All three attackers have more than 40 goal contributions, which is incredible.

A lot of credit also goes to Vincent Kompany, who has provided the right structure. As explained earlier, players like Stanisic and Alphonso Davies are playing inverted roles. This works because Bayern have strong one-on-one wingers like Luis Diaz and Michael Olise, who can take on defenders directly.

I think Olise has the potential to eventually play at Real Madrid. The way he is playing, it feels like a matter of time. Bayern, however, are building a strong project. They want to dominate and win titles consistently, including the Champions League.
They are aiming to win the Club World Cup as well. The rest of the things don’t matter as much.
